source: CAAN SMS Procedure Manual - Appendix 10 (ICAO Annex 19 aligned)

questions.text: Is there a documented safety policy, signed by the Accountable Executive, that demonstrates a positive safety culture and commitment to the SMS?
questions.guidance: The policy should be endorsed at the highest level of the organisation and reviewed periodically to remain current.

questions.text: Is the safety policy communicated effectively to all personnel and made accessible throughout the organisation?
questions.guidance: Evidence may include induction briefings, intranet postings, notice boards, and training records.

questions.text: Are safety accountabilities and responsibilities for key safety positions defined and documented (Accountable Executive, Safety Manager, postholders)?
questions.guidance: Roles, authorities, and reporting lines should be described in the SMS manual or organisational charts.

questions.text: Are key safety personnel appointed, competent, and provided with the resources needed to discharge their safety duties?
questions.guidance: Verify appointment letters, competency records, and resource allocation for the safety function.

questions.text: Is the emergency response plan (ERP) coordinated with relevant stakeholders, documented, and exercised periodically?
questions.guidance: Check ERP documentation, coordination arrangements with external agencies, and exercise/test records.

questions.text: Is the SMS documented in a controlled manner, including the SMS manual, procedures, and records management?
questions.guidance: Verify document control, versioning, and accessibility of SMS documentation and records.

questions.text: Is a formal process in place for proactive, reactive, and predictive hazard identification across the operation?
questions.guidance: Assess the completeness of hazard identification sources and the process for capturing hazards.

questions.text: Are hazard and safety reporting channels accessible to all personnel, confidential, and supported by a just culture?
questions.guidance: Verify reporting channels, confidentiality protections, and non-punitive reporting policy.

questions.text: Is a documented risk assessment process used that determines severity and probability for each identified hazard?
questions.guidance: Check risk assessment records, the risk matrix used, and consistency of ratings.

questions.text: Are risk controls and mitigations defined, assigned, implemented, and tracked to closure?
questions.guidance: Verify mitigation plans, ownership, timelines, and closure/verification records.

questions.text: Is safety risk management applied to operational changes, new services, products, and organisational changes?
questions.guidance: Assess whether a formal management-of-change / safety assessment process is followed.

questions.text: Is a safety risk register maintained, reviewed periodically, and used to support management decision-making?
questions.guidance: Verify the risk register's completeness, review cadence, and use in management reviews.

questions.text: Are safety performance indicators (SPIs) and targets defined, measured, and reviewed to monitor safety performance?
questions.guidance: Verify SPI definitions, data sources, measurement frequency, and review of results.

questions.text: Are internal SMS audits conducted in accordance with an approved schedule and audit procedures?
questions.guidance: Check audit schedules, audit reports, auditor competency, and follow-up of findings.

questions.text: Is the SMS reviewed periodically by senior management, with findings and actions documented?
questions.guidance: Verify management review meeting minutes, attendance, and action tracking.

questions.text: Are safety events investigated using appropriate analysis methods, with root causes identified and corrective actions implemented?
questions.guidance: Assess investigation procedures, analysis methods, and effectiveness of corrective actions.

questions.text: Is there a process to capture audit findings, investigation outcomes, and lessons learned to drive continuous improvement of the SMS?
questions.guidance: Verify the linkage between assurance outputs and SMS improvements.

questions.text: Are SMS training and education programmes delivered to all personnel appropriate to their roles?
questions.guidance: Check training curriculum, delivery records, and refresher training for safety-critical roles.

questions.text: Are safety briefings and safety communications delivered regularly to promote awareness and understanding of the SMS?
questions.guidance: Verify the frequency and content of safety communications and briefings.

questions.text: Are mechanisms in place to promote, measure, and continuously improve the safety culture (e.g., safety culture surveys, just culture policies)?
questions.guidance: Assess culture measurement activities and actions taken from survey results.

questions.text: Are lessons learned and safety information disseminated across the organisation to support learning and improvement?
questions.guidance: Verify dissemination of safety information, bulletins, and lessons-learned communications.
